docs.contenu:
🎯 Objectives
By the end of this lesson you will be able to:
- Use the past simple to talk about finished actions in the past.
- Form regular and irregular verbs in the past.
- Make negatives and questions with "did".
- Compare two things using comparative adjectives.

🔍 Warm-up
Read: "Yesterday I watched a film. It was more interesting than the book." This sentence contains a past action (watched) and a comparison (more interesting than). This lesson covers both.

I. The past simple: uses
📘 Rule (functions)
We use the past simple for actions that started and finished in the past.
- Finished actions: I visited my grandmother last week.
- A sequence of past events: I woke up, had breakfast and went to school.
- Past states: The weather was cold yesterday.
Time markers often used: yesterday, last week, last year, ago, in 2020, when I was young.

II. Regular verbs
📏 Form (affirmative)
Add -ed to the base verb.
- work → worked, play → played, watch → watched.
📏 Spelling rules
1. Most verbs: add -ed. clean → cleaned.
2. Verbs ending in -e: add only -d. like → liked, live → lived.
3. Consonant + y: change y to i, add -ed. study → studied, carry → carried.
4. Short verbs ending consonant-vowel-consonant: double the last consonant. stop → stopped, plan → planned.

✏️ Worked examples
- I played tennis last Saturday.
- She studied all evening.
- We stopped at the shop.

III. Irregular verbs
📘 Rule
Many common verbs do NOT take -ed. You must learn their past forms by heart.
📏 Common irregular verbs
- be → was / were
- go → went
- have → had
- do → did
- see → saw
- eat → ate
- take → took
- make → made
- come → came
- get → got
- give → gave
- write → wrote
- read → read (spelling same, pronunciation changes)
- buy → bought
- think → thought

✏️ Worked examples
- I went to the beach yesterday.
- They had a great time.
- She saw an interesting film.

👀 Note (was / were)
The past of "to be" has two forms:
- I / He / She / It → was.
- You / We / They → were.
Example: I was tired. They were happy.

IV. Negatives and questions
📏 Form (negative)
subject + did not (didn't) + base verb
- I didn't watch TV.
- She didn't go out.
⚠️ After "didn't" the verb goes back to its BASE form (no -ed, no irregular past).
Wrong: I didn't went. Right: I didn't go.

📏 Form (questions)
Did + subject + base verb ?
- Did you enjoy the party? — Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.
- What did you do yesterday?
- Where did they go?

👀 Note
"was / were" do not use "did". 
- Were you at home? — Yes, I was.
- She wasn't happy. They weren't ready.

🛠️ Method: putting a sentence into the past
Step 1 — Find the main verb.
Step 2 — Is it regular? Add -ed (watch changes to watched). Is it irregular? Use its special form (go changes to went).
Step 3 — For negatives/questions, use did/didn't + BASE verb.

V. Comparatives
📘 Rule (grammar)
Comparative adjectives compare TWO things. We usually add "than".
📏 Form
1. Short adjectives (one syllable): add -er. tall → taller, old → older, fast → faster.
2. Short adjectives ending consonant-vowel-consonant: double the consonant. big → bigger, hot → hotter.
3. Adjectives ending in -y: change y to i, add -er. happy → happier, easy → easier.
4. Long adjectives (two or more syllables): use "more" + adjective. interesting → more interesting, expensive → more expensive.
5. Irregular: good → better, bad → worse, far → further.

✏️ Worked examples
- My brother is taller than me.
- This book is more interesting than that one.
- Today is hotter than yesterday.
- Her results are better than mine.

🛠️ Method: comparing two things
Step 1 — Count the syllables of the adjective.
Step 2 — Short? Add -er. Long? Use "more".
Step 3 — Add "than" before the second thing.

⚠️ Common mistakes
1. Double comparative: more taller → taller (never use "more" with -er).
2. Forgetting "than": She is older me → She is older than me.
3. Past after "did": Did you saw...? → Did you see...?
4. Adding -ed to irregular verbs: I goed → I went.

⭐ Recap
- Past simple = finished past actions; markers: yesterday, last week, ago.
- Regular verbs add -ed; irregular verbs have special forms.
- Negatives/questions use did/didn't + base verb (but was/were do not use "did").
- Comparatives: -er for short adjectives, "more" for long ones, always with "than".

📘 Language bank
Time markers: yesterday, last night, last week, last year, two days ago, in 2019, when I was young.
Irregular verbs: was/were, went, had, did, saw, ate, took, made, came, got, bought, thought.
Adjectives: tall, short, big, small, old, young, fast, slow, easy, difficult, interesting, expensive.
Useful sentences: I watched a good film yesterday. / Did you go out last weekend? / She didn't come to school. / This exercise is easier than that one. / Football is more popular than tennis.

📝 Practice
Exercise 1 — Write the past simple of these verbs.
play → ______ ; go → ______ ; study → ______ ; have → ______ ; stop → ______ ; see → ______ ; buy → ______ ; be (I) → ______ .

Exercise 2 — Complete in the past simple.
1. Yesterday I (watch) ______ a good film.
2. She (not / go) ______ to school last Monday.
3. ______ you (visit) ______ your grandmother last week?
4. They (have) ______ a great time at the party.
5. We (be) ______ very tired after the trip.

Exercise 3 — Compare using the comparative.
1. A car / fast / a bike.
2. This book / interesting / that one.
3. Today / hot / yesterday.
4. Maths / difficult / English (for me).

✅ Answers
Exercise 1: played, went, studied, had, stopped, saw, bought, was.
Exercise 2: 1. watched 2. didn't go 3. Did ... visit 4. had 5. were.
Exercise 3: 1. A car is faster than a bike. 2. This book is more interesting than that one. 3. Today is hotter than yesterday. 4. Maths is more difficult than English for me.

🗣️ Speaking task
Tell a partner about last weekend. Use at least five past verbs (I went, I played, I watched...) and one comparison (Saturday was better than Sunday).

👀 Extra note
Two golden rules from this lesson:
1. After did / didn't, the verb goes back to its BASE form: Did you go? / I didn't go (never "Did you went").
2. Short adjectives take -er (taller), long adjectives take "more" (more interesting), and both use "than". Never combine them (never "more taller").

📋 Summary
- The past simple describes actions that started and finished in the past (yesterday, last week, ago).
- Regular verbs add -ed (worked, studied); irregular verbs have special forms (went, had, saw) that must be learned by heart.
- Negatives and questions use did/didn't + the BASE verb: I didn't go, Did you see...?
- The verb "to be" in the past is was/were and does NOT use "did": I was, they were, Was she...?
- Comparative adjectives compare two things: short adjectives take -er + than (taller than); long adjectives take more + adjective + than (more interesting than).
- Never combine both forms (never "more taller"); learn irregular comparatives by heart: good→better, bad→worse, far→further.
- Typical time markers for this chapter: yesterday, last week, two days ago, when I was young.
- Always check the -ed spelling rules (consonant doubling, y→i) before writing a paragraph in the past.
